item.title: Luai: ‘My focus now is Samoa’
item.description: Jerome Luai will be calling Papua New Guinea home in 2028- but right now- his focus is doing well for Toa Samoa in the Rugby League World Cup. The Parramatta-bound play maker said this after touching down in Port Moresby, eyes fixed on playing against PNG Kumuls this Saturday at the Santos National Football Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
Jerome Luai will be calling Papua New Guinea home in 2028- but right now- his focus is doing well for Toa Samoa in the Rugby League World Cup.

The Parramatta-bound play maker said this after touching down in Port Moresby, eyes fixed on playing against PNG Kumuls this Saturday at the Santos National Football Stadium.

Despite a big 78-4 win over France last weekend, Luai says they won’t be taking the Kumuls lightly.

“With how the pool system is set up, we can’t afford to lose, and we are looking to face the Kumuls in a strong match, in front of their home crowd,” Luai said.

“They (Kumuls) are tough to beat in their home town.

“They (Kumuls) know how to adapt in such conditions so we’re looking forward to the challenge.”

Making it to the Rugby League World Cup final in the last edition, the former Penrith Panthers premiership winning five-eighth believes the current Toa Samoa team has the depth to go an extra mile.

“I think this team (Samoa) is much better than that team respectfully and we have a few tough games coming up so we have to be locked in in every game.” he added.

item.title: Sir Puka supports Bougainville Referendum
item.description: Member for Abau, Sir Puka Temu, has openly declared his support for the Bougainville Referendum during today’s parliamentary debate. Married to a Bougainville woman and father of three, Sir Puka drew on his personal ties and the region’s history to emphasize on the legitimacy of Bougainville’s long struggle for autonomy.
item.content:encoded:
Member for Abau, Sir Puka Temu, has openly declared his support for the Bougainville Referendum during today’s parliamentary debate.

Married to a Bougainville woman and father of three, Sir Puka drew on his personal ties and the region’s history to emphasize on the legitimacy of Bougainville’s long struggle for autonomy.

He recalled the Sandline crisis and paid tribute to the courage of Bougainville women who stood firm during times of conflict, stressing that their resilience continues to shape Bougainville’s pursuit of self-determination.

Sir Puka says that Bougainville’s history of sacrifice and perseverance must be respected as the nation approaches the referendum vote.

item.title: Wanuma people in Middle Ramu set to get road access
item.description: People in the newly created Wanuma Local Level Government of Middle Ramu District can now look forward to having road accessibility into the provincial capital after 51 years of being neglected by successive governments and leaders. Wanuma was gazetted last year as the fifth LLG for Middle Ramu after Arabaka, Simbai, Kovon and Josephstaal, following a successful submission by the local MP, Kansol
item.content:encoded:
People in the newly created Wanuma Local Level Government of Middle Ramu District can now look forward to having road accessibility into the provincial capital after 51 years of being neglected by successive governments and leaders.

Wanuma was gazetted last year as the fifth LLG for Middle Ramu after Arabaka, Simbai, Kovon and Josephstaal, following a successful submission by the local MP, Kansol Harwai Kamdaru.

Construction work on its council chambers is underway and nearing completion.

Wanuma is located along the southern slopes of the Adelbert Range and was formerly part of Josephstaal LLG.

This neglected LLG sits between Madang, Sumkar, and Middle Ramu districts, and it is almost 4,000 population constitutes of people from all three electorates.

Their only means of reaching Madang Town to access basic government services or sell their cash crops like cocoa, coffee, betelnut, and tobacco plus garden produce is by trekking two to three days into Transgogol, for those on the Madang border areas, whilst those on the Sumkar sidewalk several hours down to Malas or Bunabun, where they then get on a PMV into town.

The local people said that their struggles for road connectivity plus other basic services often force them to cast their votes in all three electorates during national elections, hoping their problems would be addressed.

Their efforts, however; continue to go unnoticed by successive leaders and governments.

This prompted Middle Ramu MP, Kansol Harwai Kamdaru to make a submission for Wanuma to have its own LLG.

"The primary reason they had to be separated from Josephstaal was because they are too far away from Josephstaal and often missed out on basic government services.

"Having their own LLG gives them the power to make their own decisions and manage their own affairs," Kamdaru said.

Last Saturday, MP Kamdaru flew by helicopter to Wanuma and met with the local people.

He assured them that road works to Wanuma have begun under an interdistrict arrangement between Sumkar and Middle Ramu districts.

Mr Kamdaru also presented a million-kina cheque to the contractor, Lani Moka, owner of Roke Civil Works Ltd that is working on the road, starting from Malas to Hatitau wards 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 in Wanuma LLG.

The contractor was engaged by Sumkar DDA.

The road maintenance and construction is an initiative of Sumkar District Development Authority, under the leadership of MP, Alex Suguman.

It is a ringroad that will cut through Wanuma and back to Wanambre, Inion, and Bunabun in the Sumglibar LLG of Sumkar district.

Kamdaru stated that Middle Ramu DDA has provided the K1m counter funding to assist in completing the 78.8 kilometers road, a much- needed infrastructure that will enable his Wanuma people to access other basic services as well as boost their economic activities.

"You have missed out on a lot of services in the last 51 years and this is an opportunity that we must embrace. Middle Ramu is a big district that shares borders with Madang, Bogia, Sumkar and Usino/ Bundi districts and provinces like Western Highlands Jiwaka, Enga and East Sepik. Developing Middle Ramu is a mammoth task. We can't expect it to change in five years.

"The development challenges that we are facing today are legacy issues, and we must all work together to achieve our development goals," he added.

He further extended his appreciation to Sumkar MP and the Member for Usino/ Bundi, Vincent Kumura for assisting him and his people through such partnership arrangements, especially in road connectivity.

Middle Ramu is the only district in Madang Province that is still lacking road accessibility into the provincial capital, a challenge that Kamdaru is seriously taking on.

Wanuma LLG President, Amandi Gurunan thanked MP Kamdaru for visiting his people.

He said that Mr Kamdaru was the first MP to visit the Wanuma people, a gesture that his people highly appreciated.

Middle Ramu DDA, meanwhile; has also bought a Lucas sawmill for the Wanuma people, which Kamdaru handed over to them on Saturday.

They will use the sawmill to mill timbers for new classrooms and teachers' houses at the local primary school, community health posts and church buildings.

He also told them that building materials for a new double classroom for their school were ready and would be flown in any time funding is available for freight costs

item.title: Bougainville under drought alert
item.description: Bougainville remains under drought-alert status, with the impacts of the current El Niño weather pattern already being felt across the region and several communities in North Bougainville reaching emergency thresholds. Director of the Bougainville Disaster and Emergency Directorate, Julius Nohu, says monitoring data collected from communities shows worsening conditions in the north, where shortage
item.content:encoded:
Bougainville remains under drought-alert status, with the impacts of the current El Niño weather pattern already being felt across the region and several communities in North Bougainville reaching emergency thresholds.

Director of the Bougainville Disaster and Emergency Directorate, Julius Nohu, says monitoring data collected from communities shows worsening conditions in the north, where shortages of water and food are becoming increasingly severe.

Nohu says while some parts of Bougainville have recently received rain, the region remains under the influence of El Niño, which can bring a mix of extreme weather conditions including drought, heavy rainfall and cyclones.

He says assessments indicate that eight out of ten communities surveyed have already reached critical drought thresholds, with around 70 percent of assessed areas showing signs of agricultural stress.

The impacts are now spreading beyond agriculture and affecting water, sanitation and public health.

Nohu says health facilities in North Bougainville are reporting cases of diarrhoea, respiratory illnesses and other water-borne diseases, although no drought-related deaths have been reported so far.

The Directorate's immediate focus is on North Bougainville, where rapid assessments are underway across all Community Government areas.

Particular concern remains for Pinapel Island and the Atolls, where remoteness and limited access to services has seen the situation already deteriorating.

Nohu says emergency support is urgently needed, including water supplies for schools and health facilities, relief assistance for affected islands, and the pre-positioning of food and non-food items for vulnerable communities.

However, he says the Directorate is struggling to move beyond assessments because of funding and resource constraints.

Julius Nohu says the Bougainville Executive Council has already approved an El Niño Preparedness and Response Plan that runs through to 2027, together with an allocated budget, but implementation requires immediate financing and support from all sectors of government, development partners and the National Government.

He acknowledged the North Bougainville District Development Authority for funding assessment work across the district and is calling on other district administrations to also support response efforts.

The Directorate has already activated a multi-sector operational coordination group involving government agencies and development partners, while an Emergency Operations Centre has also been established to focus solely on El Niño operations.

Nohu warned that forecasts indicate El Niño conditions are expected to peak in November and December, making the coming weeks critical.

He says more support is needed now to rehabilitate damaged water systems, drill boreholes, refill tanks at schools and health facilities, support farmers and position emergency supplies before conditions worsen.

Nohu is also urging communities not to panic but to prepare early and responsibly.

He encouraged people to listen to radio awareness messages, keep drinking water sources clean, protect water tanks and storage containers from contamination, and pay special attention to children, the elderly and other vulnerable people.

For farmers, he says drought-tolerant crops that remain in gardens should be protected and preserved, while families should consider food storage and preservation methods to strengthen household food security.

He also warned that regional drought conditions in parts of Asia could affect rice supply chains and lead to increases in store goods prices, encouraging families to prepare ahead where possible.

Nohu says schools should continue operating safely under guidance issued by the Education Department, including reduced school hours and minimum hygiene standards.

He further warned seafarers to take extra precautions during the current weather conditions after several recent maritime incidents across the region, including vessels that drifted for weeks before rescue and another boat that remains missing.

Nohu says bad weather conditions have also disrupted maritime transport links to the Atolls, leaving some island communities unable to reach Buka, raising concerns that trade store food supplies may be running low.

He reiterated a call by Community Government Minister Milton Tukana for development partners, government agencies and communities to work together to protect those most at risk, particularly families with many children, the elderly and remote island populations.

Julius Nohu says Bougainville remains under drought-alert status, with the next assessment from the National Weather Service expected next month to determine whether the region remains on alert or progresses to emergency status.

item.title: Maladina defends development forum
item.description: Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina has hit back on critics about the millions of kinas spent to host the recent Papua LNG Development Forum in Port Moresby, saying the government has nothing to hide. He says the funding was necessary to progress the final investment decision for the project.
item.content:encoded:
Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina has hit back on critics about the millions of kinas spent to host the recent Papua LNG Development Forum in Port Moresby, saying the government has nothing to hide.

He says the funding was necessary to progress the final investment decision for the project.

Cabinet had approved K112 million to host the development forum.

Finance Minister Thomas Opa revealed that only K80 million was spent.

This has sparked public debate, with citizens and leaders questioning how the funds were used, following reports some landowners missed out on accommodation and allowances.

Responding to these concerns, Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina maintains that Papua LNG is a crucial project expected to generate billions into the national purse.

Prime Minister James Marape also defended the K80 million spent, saying it was less than what the then Somare government had invested to commence the project.

Both leaders were responding to Opposition Leader James Nomane who questioned in Parliament how the K80 million was spent and demanded accountability.

item.title: PM calls for sensitivity
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape in his opening speech on the 2019 Referendum issue in parliament today reminded members on the sensitivity of the matter. He also stressed that while all the members discuss and further decide on Bougainville's future, the outcome must be a win win for both PNG and Bougainville.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape in his opening speech on the 2019 Referendum issue in parliament today reminded members on the sensitivity of the matter.

He also stressed that while all the members discuss and further decide on Bougainville's future, the outcome must be a win win for both PNG and Bougainville.

The debate continues tomorrow allowing members to contribute to the discussion.

PM Marape said because it is very important, they have suspended question time and will speak again tomorrow.

“There'll be only one business for the petroleum minister tomorrow. But we'll go through this matter and subject to concurrence with the autonomous Bougainville leadership, we'll decide on a date in which we will take a vote on this one.”

“Let's ponder on some of this discussion and let's find something that doesn't hurt Bougainville's aspiration for self-determination but at the same time assists me and future Prime Ministers the ability to hold this diversity called Papua New Guinea together.” PM Marape said.

item.title: Makiba urges Parliament
item.description: Parliament has been urged to carefully balance the wishes of the people of Bougainville with PNG constitutional responsibilities and national interests. Minister for Bougainville Affairs Manasseh Makiba said this, when opening the debate in parliament, today.
item.content:encoded:
Parliament has been urged to carefully balance the wishes of the people of Bougainville with PNG constitutional responsibilities and national interests.

Minister for Bougainville Affairs Manasseh Makiba said this, when opening the debate in parliament, today.

The 2019 Bougainville Referendum has taken center stage in the national parliament.

Minister Makiba opened the debate today, after tabling the 2019 Referendum Results, the Joint Consultation Report and the Melanesian Framework on August 27, last year.

He reminded fellow colleagues that this debate is an important opportunity for them to consider the history, constitutional framework, the wishes of the people of Bougainville and the implications of the decision, that parliament is being asked to make.

Makiba emphasized that the vote requires a three – quarters majority, making it a substantive parliamentary and constitutional decision.

In the 2019 Referendum, 97.7 percent of Bougainvilleans voted for independence while 2.3 percent favored autonomy.

The Minister believes Bougainville deserves independence , when the timing is right.

item.title: Daio health center receives solar water pump as water tank dry

item.content:encoded:
As the El Niño conditions continue to affect everyday life, essential services, like healthcare, are also feeling the impact as prolonged dry weather worsens water shortages. ‎ ‎Daio Health Centre, a Catholic-run health facility located across the bay from Alotau Town, Milne Bay Province, had struggled to maintain basic health services until two weeks ago, when it received assistance in a form of a solar-powered water pump.

To continue providing basic health services at Daio health facility, staffs were forced to collect water from a nearby creek to care for their patients and families.‎ ‎However, the situation has been improved following a donation of a solar-powered water pump to the health facility two weeks ago, easing the burden of collecting water manually from the creek.

Secretary of Catholic Health Services of the Alotau Diocese, Sr Nomita Rozario, says the solar water pump was originally for Alotau Catholic Diocese from the National Catholic Health Services, however, considering the challenges encountered by Daio health center, the pump was gifted to them to address their water needs.

‎Sr Nomita says with assistance of the local community, the solar powered water pump was successfully installed allowing the health facility to draw water directly from the tanks. ‎ ‎The water tanks at the health facility have now been fully refilled allowing services to flow smoothly. ‎
